Article Title: 'Nothing to unite': BJP calls Congress' Karnataka Bharat Jodo Yatra 'misleading'
Article Text:
Karnataka BJP leaders B Y Vijayendra criticised the Congress’ second Bharat Jodo foot march

NEW DELHI: The Karnataka BJP on Tuesday criticised the Congress’ second ‘Bharat Jodo’ foot march, calling it “misleading” and alleging that public money was being used to benefit party workers.Karnataka BJP president B Y Vijayendra alleged that the Congress government was spending taxpayers’ money on its guarantee implementation committees and would now spend Rs 10 lakh for each gram panchayat for the Bharat Jodo programme.“First of all, they are not implementing any guarantee schemes. It has become an election gimmick for the Congress government, whether it is the Gruha Lakshmi scheme or any other scheme. They have appointed guarantee implementation committee chairpersons for each of the 224 taluks in Karnataka, and they are being paid salaries. Taxpayers' money is being spent to maintain these Congress workers," he said."Now, there is another drama called the Bharat Jodo Yatra . The Congress government is going to spend Rs 10 lakh for each Gram Panchayat for the Bharat Jodo Yatra. Where will this money come from? Again, it is taxpayers' money.Deputy chief minister Parameshwara has directly told all district commissioners to accept the list of Bharat Jodo members submitted by the guarantee committee chairpersons. This means the Rs 10 lakh will be given to Congress workers...” he added.Leader of opposition in the Karnataka assembly Chalavadi Narayanaswamy also alleged that the organisations being given the funds were effectively Congress booth-level committees.“Bharat Jodo is misleading the people because there is nothing to unite in Bharat. Bharat has always been united. In Karnataka, in the name of Bharat Jodo, ₹10 lakh is being given to each organisation, but that organisation is nothing but a booth-level committee of the Congress party. I have learned that youngsters from other parties also wanted to join these committees, but the Congress does not want to include youths from outside the party. Therefore, these are effectively booth-level committees of the Congress party. This is a deception by the Congress party and the Congress government in Karnataka...” Narayanaswamy said.The Congress is set to launch its second ‘Bharat Jodo’ foot march in Karnataka on September 30, covering all 84 Assembly constituencies where it lost in the 2023 elections. The 84-day programme will span 29 districts and begin from Shikaripura in Shivamogga district, the Assembly constituency represented by Vijayendra.Karnataka Congress chief B K Hariprasad said the march was being organised to mark four years since Rahul Gandhi’s Bharat Jodo Yatra entered Karnataka on September 30, 2022. The programme will begin with a public meeting and will subsequently cover the remaining constituencies from October 4-5 onwards.Congress has said the choice of Shikaripura was intended to highlight what it describes as shortcomings in BJP programmes. The party also plans to use the march to raise awareness about the functioning of constitutional institutions.
Article Summary: The Congress is set to launch its second ‘Bharat Jodo’ foot march in Karnataka on September 30, covering all 84 Assembly constituencies where it lost in the 2023 elections. The 84-day programme will span 29 districts and begin from Shikaripura in Shivamogga district, the Assembly constituency represented by Vijayendra.

Article Title: ‘CJP should become Istifa Janata Party’: Athawale mocks party over calls for resignations
Article Text:
Athawale takes swipe at CJP, says it keeps demanding resignations (Image credit: PTI)

NEW DELHI: Union minister Ramdas Athawale on Tuesday said the Cockroach Janata Party ( CJP ) should change its name to ‘Istifa Janata Party’, alleging that it repeatedly demands the resignation of public figures.Addressing a press conference in Guwahati, Athawale said the party was now seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, after earlier demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak."The CJP keeps asking only for resignations. They should change its name to Istifa Janata Party," said Athawale, the Union minister of state for social justice and empowerment.Athawale also commented on CJP founder Abhijit Dipke, saying he had recently entered politics, while Athawale had been working on issues concerning Dalits and other backward classes for a long time."Dipke is from Maharashtra, is a Buddhist and a Dalit. He studied in the US and is new to the field. We are aware of the various issues facing the nation, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi is sincerely working hard to resolve them," Athawale, who is also president of the Republican Party of India (Athawale), said.The minister also asserted that PM Modi would return to power for a fourth consecutive term in 2029. Referring to Assam’s development, Athawale said infrastructure had grown under PM Modi’s leadership."The initiatives taken by the prime minister have resulted in improved facilities and greater convenience for the people of the state," he said.During his visit to Assam, Athawale attended the inauguration of Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Bhavan at Chapar in Dhubri district as the chief guest. He said he interacted with local residents and elected representatives and paid floral tributes at a statue of Ambedkar.Athawale expressed hope that the building would become a centre for social justice, equality, education, social awareness and the empowerment of marginalised communities."It is my heartfelt wish that the building plays a pivotal role in spreading Babasaheb’s ideals to every individual," he said.
Article Summary: Union minister Ramdas Athawale says Cockroach Janata Party ( CJP) should change its name to 'Istifa Janata party' He says CJP keeps asking only for resignations. CJP founder Abhijit Dipke is a Buddhist and a Dalit, he says.

Article Title: Assam Rifles jawan killed, four injured in suspected militant attack along Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh
Article Text:
Suspected militant attack along India-Myanmar border (ANI file photo)

NEW DELHI: An Assam Rifles jawan was killed and four others injured after a patrol team came under suspected militant attack along the India-Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district on Tuesday, news agency PTI cited officials.The incident took place around 6.30am near Nampong Nallah under Nampong circle, when personnel of the 21 Assam Rifles were patrolling an area where border fencing work is under way.Preliminary reports suggested that suspected militants opened fire on the patrol team, killing Havildar Jankhokai Kuki, 42, and injuring four others.The injured personnel were being evacuated for medical treatment.Details about their condition were not immediately available.Security forces have intensified operations in the area following the attack, officials said.Preliminary reports indicated the involvement of militants belonging to the NSCN (K-YA), though there was no official confirmation about the identity of the attackers.An official statement from the Assam Rifles is awaited.Changlang SP Kirli Padu said police had received information about the incident and directed the officer-in-charge of Changlang police station to gather details."We have received information about the incident that took place along the India-Myanmar border and have asked the OC of Changlang police station to collect information related to it," Padu said.The India-Myanmar border in Changlang district has remained sensitive because of the movement of insurgent groups operating in the region and across the international boundary.
Article Summary: An Assam Rifles jawan was killed and four others injured after a patrol team came under suspected militant attack. The incident took place along the India- Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district. Security forces have intensified operations in the area following the attack.

NEW DELHI: In view of a "series of deeply disturbing" egregious crimes against girls and women in Delhi, Supreme Court Monday said it was a systemic failure on the part of Delhi govt and police that they can't provide a safe and secure environment to the public, which is their basic fundamental right, and sought an explanation from the authorities.Referring to the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park, the gang rape and murder of a girl in Swaroop Nagar, and the sexual assault of a girl inside a moving bus that covered a distance of over 47km from Greater Noida to Delhi, SC said that these have raised serious concerns about the safety and security of public spaces in and around the city, and took suo motu cognisance and registered a case. "The right to live with dignity, free from the fear of violence, is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental guarantee of life and personal liberty enshrined under Article 21 of Constitution," a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Chandran said.Also read: 'No basic public safety, expressing solidarity no solution': SC pulls up system amid rising rape cases in Delhi "Public spaces, including parks, roads, buses, Metro stations, subways, foot bridges, etc, cannot be permitted to become zones of high risk due to grossly inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lax patrolling, or other preventable administrative deficiencies," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Monday said it was a systemic failure on the part of Delhi govt and police that they can't provide a safe and secure environment to the public. Article Title: 'LPU targeted after owner joined BJP': Ex-Punjab CM Channi alleges political motive behind unrest
Article Text:
A series of videos from LPU captured the chaos that unfolded during student protests with footage showing a highway blockade, clashes with police, lathicharge and vehicles being set on fire.

Channi seeks answers over students, losses

Congress attacks govt's response

Police say dialogue was used to defuse tension

Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi has alleged that the protests and violence at Lovely Professional University (LPU) were politically motivated. He claimed the university came under pressure after its founder, Ashok Mittal, joined the BJP Channi also questioned the police response to the unrest and alleged that outsiders entered the campus and took part in the violence."Outsiders went there and engaged in hooliganism. This hooliganism was sponsored by the Police themselves. LPU Founder Ashok Mittal has joined the BJP, and after that, the Aam Aadmi Party government has tried to destroy this University," Channi said.He repeated his allegation that people from outside the university later entered the campus and created trouble."After that, what happened, people from outside came and engaged in hooliganism there," he said.Channi also questioned reports that the university suffered financial losses of around Rs 100 crore during the unrest, while stressing that he could not confirm the figure himself."A loss of around 100 crore rupees, as reported—I don't know for sure—has occurred, so who is responsible?" he asked.He further alleged that students were subjected to excessive force and questioned why action had not been taken against police personnel accused of assaulting them."And after that, students were beaten up severely; who is responsible for that? Why was no action taken against those police officers and personnel who beat up the students so brutally? And why was the situation not handled in time?" he said.Former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa also criticised the government's handling of the situation. He said the authorities should have responded more quickly after students began protesting."What happened in LPU, the govt has acted very late...they should have acted swiftly. Students came to the street, protested. This should not work like this," Randhawa said.Randhawa also rejected State Railway Minister Ravneet Singh Bittu's allegation that the student protest was intended to disrupt an upcoming AAP event. He said students should not be portrayed in such a manner."Students should not be demeaned. This is Bittu's habit to speak like this, which has no meaning. I suggest he not deliver such a statement, being the grandson of a politician, which could fracture the image of the state," he said.Congress Working Committee (CWC) member Bhawar Jitendra Singh, meanwhile, raised allegations of "vote chori" across Punjab."Complaints are being received all across the state on vote chori. He is just a chief of the ECI. But the system, BJP, which is involved in it must be discussed."Punjab director general of police Gaurav Yadav said police had exercised restraint and relied on dialogue to bring the situation under control after a large number of students gathered at LPU following "late-night rumours about certain incidents".Yadav said the unrest began during the intervening night of September 26 and 27. Students gathered on the campus, followed by some vandalism and the setting on fire of part of a gate.Senior police officers, including DIG Jalandhar Range Navin Singla and Kapurthala SSP, reached the university. Police then held discussions with students to hear their grievances against the university administration.
Article Summary: Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi has alleged that the protests and violence at Lovely Professional University (LPU) were politically motivated. He claimed the university came under pressure after its founder, Ashok Mittal, joined the BJP. Channi also questioned the police response to the unrest and alleged that outsiders entered the campus.

Article Title: Confession can't be sole ground to convict a person under NSA: SC fines UP govt Rs 10 lakh
Article Text:
Tensions escalated in Sambhal in November 2024 during a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday imposed a cost of Rs 10 lakh on the Uttar Pradesh government, holding that a confession statement by an accused cannot, by itself, form the basis for his detention under the National Security Act (NSA).Uttar Pradesh Police had invoked the NSA against Mulla Afroz in October 2025 over his alleged involvement in the 2024 communal violence in Sambhal.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu delivered the judgment while quashing Afroz’s preventive detention.The NSA empowers the Centre and state governments to detain individuals to prevent them from acting in a manner deemed “prejudicial to the defence of India”. Detention can be ordered for up to 12 months, although it can be revoked earlier.Tensions escalated in Sambhal in November 2024 during a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid, following claims that a Harihar temple had previously stood at the site.On November 24, during the second round of the survey, protesters clashed with security personnel. The violence left four people dead and dozens injured.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Police had invoked the NSA against Mulla Afroz in October 2025 over his alleged involvement in the 2024 communal violence in Sambhal. The NSA empowers the Centre and state governments to detain individuals to prevent them from acting in a manner deemed ‘prejudicial to the defence of India’

Article Title: Kanpur plane crash: No distress call, flight-monitoring gaps emerge in AAIB probe
Article Text:
A four-seater, dual-engine Tecnam aircraft crashed in a fatal crash on the outskirts of the Natthapurwa village near the Ganga Barrage in Kanpur.

No records of flight-data checks

Aircraft stopped responding after final radio call

Engines and flight data being examined

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has found that Garg Aviation did not fully follow required flight-monitoring procedures before its training aircraft crashed near Kanpur on August 27, killing an instructor and a trainee pilot.The seven-page preliminary report also recommends that the Directorate General of Civil Aviation issue clearer guidelines on how Flying Training Organisations should monitor flight data.The Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft crashed near the Ganga Barrage less than 20 minutes after taking off from Kanpur's civil aerodrome. The 39-year-old instructor and 28-year-old trainee were killed.AAIB said Garg Aviation told investigators that it carried out random checks of data from the aircraft's Garmin system. However, the operator could not provide records of those checks and did not have a Standard Operating Procedure explaining how the monitoring was conducted or what limits would trigger further action."When queried on flight data monitoring, the FTO stated that random monitoring of Garmin data was being carried out; however, no records of such monitoring were maintained, and there was no SOP defining how the monitoring was conducted or what exceedance limits were considered for it," AAIB said.The Garmin data card acts as a type of flight-data recorder for small aircraft. AAIB said interim safety recommendations were necessary and called for stricter compliance with flight-data monitoring requirements."Further, DGCA may issue specific guidelines detailing the procedure to be followed for flight data monitoring, which shall be made part of the TPM," the probe agency said. TPM refers to the Training and Procedure Manual.The aircraft, registered as VT-NBV, took off at around 11.11 am on August 27. About 14 minutes later, it made a radio call saying operations were normal and that it would contact the controller again after 10 minutes.That call never came."No further call was received from VT-NBV thereafter. The RT controller attempted to contact VT-NBV but received no response," AAIB said.The aircraft had no distress call before the crash. Garg Aviation was informed at around 12.10 pm that the plane had force-landed in the Ganga Barrage area, after which the company's team went to the site.AAIB said local residents had reported the crash through the 112 emergency helpline. Police and ambulance teams reached the site and took both occupants to a hospital in Kanpur, where they were declared dead.Investigators have recovered the Garmin data card from the wreckage and downloaded its information for analysis. Both engines have also been recovered and quarantined for detailed examination."Both engines have been retrieved and quarantined for further detailed examination. The investigation team is coordinating with the OEM for further examination," it said. OEM refers to Original Equipment Manufacturer.The investigation also involves Italy's ANSV and the US National Transportation Safety Board, which have each appointed an accredited representative. Tecnam has also provided a technical adviser.AAIB has sought documents relating to the aircraft and its operating crew from the DGCA as the investigation continues.The crash occurred at Kanpur's civil aerodrome, an uncontrolled aerodrome managed and maintained by the Airports Authority of India. An uncontrolled aerodrome does not have an operating control tower.
Article Summary: Aircraft stopped responding after final radio call. Aircraft had no distress call before the crash. Garg Aviation told investigators that it carried out random checks of data from the aircraft's Garmin system. No records of such monitoring were maintained, and there was no SOP defining how the monitoring was conducted.

Article Title: To recover fines, link traffic challans to power bills: Supreme Court
Article Text:
SC seeks new way to recover traffic fines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday asked govt to adopt an innovative approach to make traffic law violaters pay fines and suggested challans should be linked with electricity bill to force them to pay the penalty or face power disconnection.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Justice K V Viswanathan also suggested that authorities should take steps for blacklisting vehicles with unpaid challans and also block ownership transfers."It is not just sufficient to keep issuing e-challans. Police may issue thousands and lakhs of such e-challans. Question is recovery of fines as sought to be imposed by way of the e-challans...If people are not paying traffic challans, add it to their electricity dues bill. They'll have to pay electricity bills, otherwise the power line will be disconnected. Work it out. In this country, you have to find a way out," the bench said.The court was informed that challans of Rs 45,000 crore have been issued but Rs 25,000 crore has been recovered so far.It also suggested random checks of vehicles to identify those against which e-challans remained unpaid.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asks govt to adopt innovative approach to make traffic law violaters pay fines. Suggests challans should be linked with electricity bill to force them to pay penalty. Justices J B Pardiwala and Justice K V Viswanathan also suggested that authorities should take steps for blacklisting vehicles with unpaid challans.

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate on Tuesday searched the premises of former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen and others as part of a money laundering investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), officials said.The searches were carried out at 15 locations in connection with alleged financial irregularities.The ED’s investigation centres on MassArt’s activities, including its Durga Puja ‘Preview Shows’. According to agency officials, the society allegedly collected substantial sums from the public while portraying itself as a UNESCO-sponsored organisation.The agency has alleged that the funds raised through these activities were later diverted for personal gains. The money laundering probe is focused on the suspected proceeds of crime linked to the society’s financial transactions.The ED’s action under Section 17 allows the agency to search premises and seize documents or assets suspected to be connected with proceeds of crime, subject to the provisions of the PMLA.

Article Title: Ancestral home of '62 war hero in Uttarakhand to be made museum
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat's inimitable bravery in the battle of Nuranang against the advancing Chinese troops in 1962 is an indelible part of popular lore. A memorial to honour him was built by the Army at the site of his supreme sacrifice in the border region of Arunachal Pradesh.A biographical movie '72 Hours: Martyr Who Never Died' depicting his remarkable story as a soldier of the 4th battalion of Garhwal Rifles was made too. However, what remained missing was a befitting memorial to the Mahavir Chakra awardee at his ancestral village in Uttarakhand.BJP MP Anil Baluni, who represents Garhwal constituency in Lok Sabha, said the late soldier's home at Baryun village of Pauri Garhwal will be developed into a modern museum. He will perform 'bhoomi pujan' for the project on Nov 17.While the 'Jaswant Garh War Memorial' in Arunachal Pradesh is a draw for visitors and tourists, a museum at the place of his birth is expected to further cement his legacy in his home state, which sends men to the armed forces in large numbers when compared to its relatively small size.Baluni said he had met the martyred soldier's family members who consented to the initiative and appreciated the project. Rawat had enlisted in 4th Garhwal Rifles on Aug 19, 1960, at the young age of 19. He was just 21 when he laid down his life on Nov 17, 1962.
Article Summary: Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat's inimitable bravery in the battle of Nuranang against the advancing Chinese troops in 1962 is an indelible part of popular lore. Article Title: Coast Guard saves sinking tanker with 23 crew off Odisha coast
Article Text:
Indian Coast Guard

NEW DELHI: In an operation to avert a major disaster at sea, Indian Coast Guard Sunday rescued a foreign-flagged tanker carrying 23 crew members and 9,000 tonnes of palm oil after its main engine failed, ballast tanks began flooding and the vessel was dangerously tilted off Odisha coast, reports Surendra Singh.The Belize-flagged MT Seagull 9 sent out a distress call around 7.30am Sunday, when it was 37 nautical miles east-southeast of Paradip. In a post on X Monday, Indian Coast Guard (ICG) said, "... Following a critical distress call from MT Seagull 9 off Paradip, ICGS Vishwast launched a swift & decisive operation to rescue the unstable chemical tanker carrying 9,000 MT palm oil & 23 crew members." ICG said concurrent cargo transfer and de-flooding operations helped prevent the tanker from capsizing.
Article Summary: The Belize-flagged MT Seagull 9 sent out a distress call around 7.30am Sunday, when it was 37 nautical miles east-southeast of Paradip. Indian Coast Guard said concurrent cargo transfer and de-flooding operations helped prevent the tanker from capsizing.

Article Title: Opposition parties trying to vitiate country's atmosphere: BJP

BJP hits out at opposition over EC protest, alleges ‘sole agenda’ is to grab power

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday accused the opposition parties of trying to vitiate the country's atmosphere and spread chaos amid their protest against the Election Commission, alleging that the sole agenda of netas like Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and Arvind Kejriwal was to "grab power" by any means."Their toolkit mindset is at work: Level allegations, vitiate the country's atmosphere and run away," Union health and family welfare minister J P Nadda said, claiming that the EC's statement following a joint meeting of its three members had exposed the opposition's fabricated charge against the poll body and govt. "Rahul Gandhi should realise that repeating a lie a hundred times cannot make it true," he said.Opposition parties have cited an Indian Express report, which suggested that CEC Gyanesh Kumar was acting unilaterally over the implementation of SIR as it highlighted written objections from two election commissioners, to step up their attack on the commission and have demanded Kumar's resignation.BJP has seized on the EC's statement on Saturday, which said all SIR related decisions were unanimous while announcing measures to address some of the issues, to assert that it has exposed the "falsehood" of the opposition's campaign.Nadda said the people of the country had fully understood the double standards and the negative politics of the opposition. "People have taught a befitting lesson to the forces seeking to create instability in the country in the past, and will do so in the future too," he added.
Article Summary: BJP alleges ‘sole agenda’ of netas like Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and Arvind Kejriwal was to "grab power" by any means. Union health and family welfare minister J P Nadda said the EC's statement had exposed the opposition's fabricated charge against the poll body and govt.

Article Title: Cachar police arrest man over 'communally provocative’ social media posts
Article Text:
In Assam, 29-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly sharing inflammatory online content that criticized the Bajrang Dal, RSS, and Hinduism.

A 29-year-old man was detained on Monday in the Cachar region of Assam for allegedly making "communally provocative" statements on social media, according to authorities.According to the police, Kalparnab Gupta, who claims to be an IIT-Bombay research scholar and the head convenor of the Barak Union for Civil Liberties on Facebook, was taken into custody after a Bajrang Dal activist filed a complaint at the Silchar police station.The man was accused in the complaint of posting "defamatory, hateful and communally provocative content" on Facebook that was directed against the Bajrang Dal, RSS, and Hinduism.Additionally, Gupta was charged with trying to connect members of the Bajrang Dal to extortion schemes and a recent local gang rape assault.He was also accused of mocking religious symbols like "sakha-sindoor" and making derogatory statements about Lord Ram and other Hindu deities as per PTI report.According to the accusation, Gupta was also encouraging beef consumption in a way that was purportedly meant to offend religious feelings and foster conflict among the community.According to the police, Gupta has been charged under many Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita laws pertaining to inciting animosity, public mischief, and defamation, as well as the Assam Cattle Preservation Act regulations.The accused is being questioned and digital evidence is being gathered as a part of an ongoing investigation.

Article Title: 'SP, Congress ki Lanka jalaoge?' UP minister's remarks to new govt recruits spark row
Article Text:
Om Prakash Rajbhar's remarks on Congress, SP spark row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar's remarks asking newly appointed government officials to help "burn the Lanka" of the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress at a government programme on Monday sparked a political row, with the opposition accusing him of misusing a government platform to target rivals.Addressing a programme in Lucknow where appointment letters were distributed to 1,375 newly selected gram panchayat officers, Rajbhar urged the recruits to publicise the work of the Yogi Adityanath government ahead of the 2027 assembly elections."Akele Hanuman ji Lanka jala ke aa gaye the... aap bataiye to Samajwadi Party aur Congress ki Lanka jalaoge ya nahin jalaoge (Lord Hanuman had gone alone and burnt Lanka... Tell me, will you burn the Lanka of the Samajwadi Party and Congress or not?" news agency PTI quoted the minister saying.Rajbhar, who heads BJP ally Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), asked the recruits to publicise the government's work in whichever districts they are posted."Once you leave from here and join your job in whichever district you are posted, publicise this (Ab jab aap yahan se jaayenge apni naukri join karenge, jis bhi zile mein aapko milegi naukri, wahan is baat ka prachar prasar kariyega)," he said."Tell your brothers and sisters that if they also want a job without paying money, then make Yogi Adityanath the chief minister for the third time," Rajbhar added.He then asked the beneficiaries how many would "publicise" the message, following which almost all those seated on the other side of the stage raised their hands.Taking his remarks into a colloquial Purvanchali tone, Rajbhar invoked the Ramayana's account of Hanuman burning Lanka."Hanuman ji had gone alone and burnt Lanka after finding out the entire strength of Ravan and then returned to tell Lord Ram. You are 1,375 people here. Tell me, will you burn the Lanka of the Samajwadi Party and Congress or not?" he said."Do not worry, although I alone keep setting fire to their Lanka every day," Rajbhar added with a smile.The programme was attended by chief minister Yogi Adityanath, agriculture minister Surya Pratap Shahi and senior Panchayati Raj department officials.The remarks drew criticism from the Congress and SP, which accused the minister of using a government event to target political opponents.Congress state chief Ajay Rai said, "To exhort the candidates who are starting their government jobs to target Congress and Samajwadi Party is shocking. Was it a political rally or a government event. Is this how you provoke masses?"Rajbhar also attacked the opposition over its criticism of the state government's performance, saying connectivity between districts had improved, digital libraries had been established in villages and development had taken place."But the people of the Samajwadi Party and Congress say that nothing has happened. It seems the power of their glasses has become weak, which is why they cannot see anything," he said.He further said the opposition parties were engaged in politics of opposition rather than ideas."Whether they are people of the Congress or the SP, these people are actually dead people; they are not alive."They do not do politics of ideas, but only politics of opposition. They want to do politics of hatred, but the people do not want politics of hatred. They want brotherhood and mutual harmony."Rajbhar urged the gathering to ensure that the strength of the SP and Congress was halved in the 2027 elections.

The Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party on Monday accused the BJP government in Gujarat of misusing the Election Commission and police to force opposition candidates to withdraw their nomination papers or have their nominations rejected ahead of the October 11 Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation elections.The BJP rejected the allegations as "baseless" and described them as a "modus operandi" of the opposition to attack constitutional organizations.The Congress, meanwhile, submitted a memorandum to the State Election Commission alleging that the BJP was misusing government machinery and police to intimidate its candidates and their family members into withdrawing their nomination papers for the civic polls, party sources told news agency PTI.According to the memorandum, Congress candidates from civic wards 6 and 7, along with their families and relatives, were allegedly being pressured by personnel from the local crime branch and local police, including an LCB police inspector, to withdraw their nominations."Such actions amount to intimidation and an abuse of power, and they seriously jeopardise the candidates' freedom of choice," the memorandum said.The deadline for filing nominations for the October 11 polls was September 26, according to the election schedule.The AAP separately alleged that the nomination form of its candidate Jitendra Chauhan from ward number 5 was rejected "solely for political reasons".AAP chief spokesperson Karan Barot said Chauhan had submitted his nomination along with all the required documents and had received an acknowledgement confirming the submission."However, he said that his form was rejected today without warning on the grounds that the mandate was lacking," Barot said.Barot alleged that there were attempts to prevent AAP candidates from contesting the elections."If Congress candidates run and win, the underlying 'arrangement' is such that they eventually desert to the BJP—a process that the AAP does not engage in. This is the reason why the forms of one of our candidates and an independent candidate were denied," he said.He also questioned the Election Commission and accused the BJP of misusing central agencies such as the CBI and the ED.Responding to the allegations, Gujarat BJP chief spokesperson Anil Patel accused the Congress of following a "modus operandi" of making baseless allegations against constitutional institutions."Congress has made the decision to target and discredit constitutional institutions both at home and abroad. Institutions established by the Constitution should be trusted," Patel said.He said democratic elections had recently been held in several states and their results announced impartially.Patel also rejected the Congress's allegations of forced withdrawals, saying it resorted to "baseless allegations" whenever it felt it was losing an election."The Congress has little faith in its own candidates. They started with EVMs, followed by SIR, and now they are accusing the Election Commission. The ruling party also recorded victories across municipal corporations, municipalities, district panchayats and taluka panchayats, while the Congress finished second and the AAP made modest gains.The results also saw the Samajwadi Party and the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) open their accounts in Gujarat.
Article Summary: The Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party accuse the BJP government in Gujarat of misusing the Election Commission and police. NEW DELHI: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student on the university campus. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. Several policemen were injured.The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice. Heavy police deployment has been made on the campus, while students have started leaving for their homes.Classes suspended, exams postponedFollowing the violence, LPU suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice.The administration appealed to students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.Several rounds of talks between protesting students and the university management remained inconclusive.Vice Chancellor Sandhu assured students that their genuine grievances would be addressed.The protesters demanded that LPU Founder-Chancellor Ashok Mittal, who is also a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, visit the protest site and assure them that their concerns would be resolved. They also sought that access to the University Management System not be blocked and that students not be victimised for participating in the protest.A large police force led by ADGP M F Farooqui entered the LPU campus after the violence escalated. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night, Farooqui said.“We will ensure security on the campus throughout the night... A force of over 2,000 personnel is currently deployed here. Law and order has been fully maintained and restored... The process is ongoing, and we are working to keep the situation under control. I cannot provide further details at this moment. To the families whose daughters are staying in the hostel here: please do not worry; everyone is safe... The atmosphere here is completely calm, and the university students are also cooperating with us in restoring peace. ..,” he said.Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh said reports of disturbances in the hostels were rumours and that all hostels had been checked.“First of all, reports of disturbances in the hostels were merely rumours. All hostels have been checked, and there are no issues. Traffic has resumed, and the situation is normal. Other matters will be resolved through discussions with the students... Overall, the atmosphere is fine, and any minor issues will be addressed... Please inform the families that all students are safe and there is no cause for concern,” Singh said.DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla also said the situation had been brought under control and that traffic movement on NH-44 would soon be restored.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has directed strict action against those responsible for the unrest at Lovely Professional University (LPU), the Chief Minister’s Office said.Mann also directed Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav to visit the spot and assess the situation.The protest began near Girls' Hostel-3 around 1 am on Sunday after students alleged that a female student had been raped by a plumber three days earlier. They also claimed the hostel warden had been informed but no action was taken.The protesters blocked NH-44 outside the university from around 8 am, causing long queues of stranded vehicles. Police later attempted to clear the blockade, but students allegedly threw water bottles at them and clashed with personnel.Police resorted to a mild lathi charge, following which students moved towards the campus and continued to pelt stones at police vehicles. Two police vehicles were set on fire, while four to five vehicles were damaged, according to Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk.Viral videos showed damaged property, vehicles and an ATM kiosk on the campus. Some students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23UM aircraft and a military tank installed on the premises.A truck driver, Vikas Yadav, said, “We have been stranded since 7 AM; there is no sign of things opening up yet... We are extremely distressed... We have had to abandon our vehicles and flee...”Police said an FIR had been registered against an unknown person based on a complaint by the students and a special investigation team had been formed.Singla said the girl was staying in Hostel No. 3 and had returned to her home after students alleged that no action had been taken on the matter. He said the investigation would involve student representatives.“We will analyse forensic samples, CCTV camera footage, call records, etc., before reaching a conclusion,” Singla said.The DIG also said students had demanded that the hostel staff comprise only women, adding that the management would address the demand.Asked about another death, Singla said a female student from Telangana studying at LPU had died by suicide 15 days earlier. “If the students say that there was foul play, action will be taken,” he said.LPU Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said the university was not aware of any such rape incident but would cooperate with the investigation.LPU management has denied the rape allegations, with Registrar Monica Gulati saying certain “anti-social elements” were spreading “false, baseless and fabricated” claims.The university released a video featuring three female students identified as residents of Room No. 504 of the hostel. In the video, the students said no rape had taken place in their room and asked police and other students not to disturb them.Gulati introduced the video by saying, “I would like you to hear what the girls residing in room number 504 of GH3 told us.”The first student said, “So, we are the residents of room number 504. Nothing of that sort happened in our room; we have been living here for the past two months. Please, police and students, do not bother us. Nothing like that happened in our room, and we are not involved in this at all.”The second student said, “We have been extremely distressed today, and if we face further trouble, we will involve our parents. Please do not harass us.”The third added, “And the police should also stop coming to our room repeatedly; otherwise, we will call our parents.”Gulati later said, “The only conclusion to be drawn from all this is that anti-social elements and individuals with vested interests are behind this.”The opposition Congress criticised the AAP government over the law and order situation in Punjab.“What is happening at LPU is deeply concerning. If students have serious questions or concerns about any incident, they deserve transparent, impartial and time-bound answers, not rumours or suppression. The violence is a testament to the failed law and order situation in Punjab,” state Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said.“NH-44 has been blocked since the morning, yet not a single representative from the AAP government has bothered to meet the students and hear their grievances,” Warring said.
Article Summary: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night.

LUCKNOW: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Tuesday announced that she would enter politics independently, saying Uttar Pradesh was her “karmabhoomi” and the state would be the starting point of her political journey.In a video statement, Mittal said her decision grew out of what she had seen during her administrative career. “I realised that many problems of the public do not get resolved even when approvals, funds and provisions are in place,” she said. “There are people whose voices do not reach the government, and even when they do, their problems remain unheard.”She cited the example of a remote village where residents had sought a school offering education beyond Class V. Mittal said she approved the proposal, but construction had not begun years later. “It was not a question of funds or rules. There was a lack of intent,” she said.She also referred to a landless beneficiary who had official documents for an allotted plot but, she said, had not received physical possession.“Inquiries found irregularities in the reports, and corrective action was taken. Yet the work did not move forward,” Mittal said, questioning what she described as “higher-level interference” in cases where people were legally entitled to relief.Mittal said she wanted to take up issues including poor rural infrastructure, unsafe roads, examination paper leaks and employment concerns in the age of artificial intelligence. These, she said, needed greater public debate and attention from policymakers.“I want politics of intent, justice, concern and long-term thinking,” she said. “My objective is not just to replace political leaders. It is to change the way politics functions," she added.Rejecting speculation that she might join an existing party, Mittal said she would work directly with citizens and build an independent platform. She alleged that false political rumours circulated after her resignation were intended to discourage newcomers from entering public life. “I will not be deterred from raising public issues,” she said.Mittal appealed to people from different walks of life, including teachers, farmers, students, doctors, labourers and lawyers, to join her effort. “Meaningful political change can come only through collective public participation,” she said.

Article Title: 8 US Marines hurt in previously unreported Iranian strikes; possible traumatic brain injuries: Report
Article Text:
File photo: Vessel attacked in Strait of Hormuz

Marines were not aboard US Navy ship

Pentagon casualty figures under scrutiny

Eight US Marines were injured in a previously undisclosed attack in the Strait of Hormuz on September 14, NBC News reported, citing three US officials.The Marines were part of a battalion landing team when the missile hit the vessel, the officials said. Seven were enlisted personnel and one was an officer. None suffered serious injuries, but they experienced smoke inhalation and concussion-like symptoms, including headaches, with officials saying some may have sustained traumatic brain injuries.All eight returned to duty shortly after the attack, according to the officials.The vessel struck in the attack was not a US Navy ship, according to the officials, who did not identify its type and referred to it only as a maritime vessel.The Pentagon did not publicly report the September 14 attack or the injuries at the time. The eight Marines were added to the Defense Casualty Analysis System nearly 10 days after the incident.One US official attributed the delay partly to injuries such as concussion symptoms that can take time to emerge, as well as the casualty database not being updated in real time.As of Wednesday, the Pentagon database had recorded 861 US service members as injured in the war with Iran, with the eight Marines included in that tally.The disclosure comes as the Pentagon faces renewed scrutiny over how it reports US military casualties in the conflict.A Washington Post report said at least four US service members killed in the Middle East since the war began were not reflected in the official casualty count at the time. The Pentagon has also faced accusations of downplaying some injuries reported by wounded troops.The US military has disputed those allegations, saying casualty classifications such as “not seriously injured” and “combat casualty” have specific definitions that can be misunderstood.The newly reported Marine injuries add another previously undisclosed incident to the broader debate over how quickly US military casualties are recorded and publicly reported during the conflict.
Article Summary: Eight US Marines were injured in a previously undisclosed attack in the Strait of Hormuz on September 14, NBC News reported. None suffered serious injuries, but they experienced smoke inhalation and concussion-like symptoms, including headaches. The Pentagon did not publicly report the September 14 attack or the injuries at the time.

Article Title: Who was behind RAF Fairford terror plot? 'Foreign actor' claim puts Iran link in focus
Article Text:
File photo: United States Air Force personnel at RAF Fairford

Trump says plot ‘might’ be linked to Iran

What happened near RAF Fairford?

The suspected terror plot near RAF Fairford has put a possible Iran link back in focus after US secretary of state Marco Rubio said a foreign actor was “clearly” involved, without naming the country or providing evidence. The development comes as British counter-terrorism investigators continue to examine whether the five men arrested near the airbase had links to a foreign state.Rubio made the claim after five British men arrested near the US-used airbase were released on police bail and stated that the incident “clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor”.The men, all British nationals in their early 20s from London, remain under investigation and have been placed under stringent conditions governing their movement and contact with others. UK counter-terrorism police have said their release does not mean the investigation is over.US president Donald Trump also weighed in on Monday, saying he would not have released the suspects on bail.Asked whether the case was linked to Iran, Trump said: “It might.” He declined to elaborate, saying he knew the answer but preferred not to disclose it.Trump had earlier said the suspects wanted to cause “big damage” and suggested they had been under investigation by British and US authorities.British sources, however, have indicated that while the broader threat environment was known, the specific activities of the five men were not necessarily known.Iran, however, has strongly denied any involvement in the incident. The Iranian embassy in London “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” what it called “unfounded and malicious speculations” by British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Tehran to the arrest of the five suspects near RAF Fairford.The embassy said such claims, particularly following what it described as US and Israeli “criminal acts of aggression” against Iran, would only fuel “Iranophobia propaganda” in the UK. It also said Iran reserved the right to take legal measures to protect the country’s rights and interests in response to what it called misleading and damaging media narratives.Police were alerted early Sunday after a local farmer reported seeing three white vans and a group of hooded or masked men near the base.Armed officers arrested five men in the Whelford area, about a mile from RAF Fairford. They were initially held on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and were later arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act. Around 85 homes were evacuated and a 400-metre cordon was imposed while bomb-disposal teams and forensic experts examined the vehicles.An initial examination of the vans led investigators to assess whether they contained explosive materials. British media later reported that no viable explosives had been found.The head of UK Counter Terrorism Policing, assistant commissioner Laurence Taylor, said investigators were considering “multiple lines of enquiry”, including the possibility that the activity involved proxies or individuals knowingly or unknowingly working for a foreign state.The possibility of an Iranian connection has drawn particular attention because RAF Fairford has been used by US bombers in operations against Iran.Iran's Revolutionary Guards had previously warned that the base could be considered a legitimate target if it was used to launch attacks. The area has also seen increased security activity amid tensions between Britain, the US and Iran.British defence secretary Wes Streeting said Iran and its proxies were known to pose threats, while foreign secretary Ed Miliband said Britain had to be prepared to confront security threats and Iranian proxies.But neither British counter-terrorism police nor the government has publicly established that Iran was behind the Fairford incident.The investigation therefore remains open to several possibilities, with police examining whether the suspects acted independently, on behalf of a foreign state or as proxies.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio said a foreign actor was ‘clearly’ involved, without naming the country or providing evidence. The development comes as British counter-terrorism investigators continue to examine whether the five men arrested near the airbase had links to a foreign state. Iran has strongly denied any involvement in the incident.

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami , in view of the red alert issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for the next two days, spoke to Secretary Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Vinod Kumar Suman and directed all concerned districts and departments to take necessary precautionary measures.Dhami directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts, continuously monitor vulnerable areas and ensure that all arrangements for relief and rescue operations are in place in advance in case of any emergency. He also directed that district emergency operation centres remain active and weather warnings be disseminated immediately at the local level.Disaster management and rehabilitation minister Madan Kaushik also spoke to Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman and took stock of the weather situation and preparedness across the state. He directed officials to closely monitor the weather and remain fully prepared to deal with any eventuality.Following the chief minister’s directions, Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman held a meeting with all 13 districts on Friday and instructed them to remain on alert mode.According to the weather department forecast, on September 26, red alerts have been issued for five districts, orange alerts for five districts and yellow alerts for three districts.On September 27, red alerts have been issued for four districts, orange alerts for four districts and yellow alerts for five districts.On September 26, Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar are under a red alert, while Dehradun, Pauri Garhwal, Rudraprayag, Chamoli and Almora are under an orange alert. Haridwar, Uttarkashi and Tehri Garhwal are under a yellow alert.On September 27, red alerts have been issued for Dehradun, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri Garhwal and Haridwar; orange alerts for Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital and Rudraprayag; and yellow alerts for Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar and Pithoragarh.The weather department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places and extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places. Authorities have been asked to remain particularly vigilant in view of the possibility of landslides and road blockages in hilly areas, rising water levels in rivers and streams, and waterlogging in the plains.Suman directed all districts to continuously monitor vulnerable areas, keep district emergency operation centres operational and ensure immediate dissemination of every weather warning to the ground level.Officials have been instructed to continuously monitor water levels in rivers, streams, gad-gaderas and other water sources and make arrangements to shift people living nearby to safer locations if water levels rise. JCBs and other necessary machinery should be stationed at strategic locations along landslide-prone roads and areas so that blocked routes can be cleared at the earliest.All district emergency operation centres have been directed to remain operational round the clock, with continuous coordination among the police, SDRF, fire services, health, Public Works Department, drinking water, power and other concerned departments. Relief and rescue teams, along with necessary equipment and resources, should be deployed in vulnerable areas as required.The secretary also directed that traffic on mountain routes be regulated based on weather and road conditions and unnecessary travel in areas vulnerable to landslides and heavy rainfall be avoided. People living near rivers, streams and seasonal water channels should be regularly alerted and prevented from approaching riverbanks or entering fast-flowing waters.Special monitoring has also been ordered along the Char Dham routes, major tourist destinations and other vulnerable areas to ensure the safety of pilgrims and tourists. All arrangements should be kept ready in advance so that relief and rescue operations can begin with minimum response time in case of an emergency.Suman urged district administrations to remain fully alert and not to show any negligence in view of the prevailing weather conditions. He also appealed to the public to follow advisories issued by the weather department and district administration, avoid unnecessary travel and stay away from rivers, streams and landslide-prone areas.The State Emergency Operation Centre is continuously monitoring the weather situation. In case of any emergency, people can contact the State Emergency Operation Centre at toll-free number 1070, the District Emergency Operation Centre at 1077, or emergency services at 112.

He directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts. Suman urged district administrations to remain fully alert and not to show any negligence in view of the prevailing weather conditions.

Article Title: 'Want to score well': Friend says Sahil Wakode told her in 'last call' he was caught cheating
Article Text:
According to police, Wakode told her during the call that his thermodynamics theory paper had gone poorly.





MUMBAI: The Mumbai crime branch probing the abetment to suicide of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode has recorded the statement of a friend, who told investigators that she was the last person to speak to him on the phone.According to police, Wakode told her during the call that his thermodynamics theory paper had gone poorly and that he was worried as he had wanted to score well. He also told her that he had been caught cheating during the exam, they said.The friend, who is among at least six students whose statements have been recorded so far, told police that Wakode appeared stressed during their conversation. However, investigators have so far not found any clear indication of stress or distress in the material examined during the probe.Wakode (22), a second-year BTech student, was found dead in his hostel room hours after the exam on Sept 18.Investigators are reconstructing his movements after he left the exam hall. CCTV footage has established that Wakode left the hall after he was asked to do so and returned later.The CCTV footage has been sent for forensic analysis. Investigators are also examining Wakode’s locked iPhone, hoping to retrieve his last calls, messages and other data.Experts have so far been unable to access the phone because of its password.Police said they are currently recording the statements of students and other witnesses and will subsequently record the statement of Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, who was present during the exam.Wakode’s parents made an emotional appeal to IIT-B students to continue their protest and sought preservation of any evidence relating to the death. In another video message addressed to students, Wakode’s father said on Sunday he had been unable to enter the campus despite visiting it two or three times. He reiterated that he planned to begin a hunger strike at Azad Maidan from Monday, demanding access to the institute and justice for his son.
Article Summary: Mumbai crime branch probing the abetment to suicide of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode has recorded the statement of a friend. Wakode (22), a second-year BTech student, was found dead in his hostel room hours after the exam on Sept 18.

Article Title: Toll soars to 81 as UP is lashed by 775% excess rainfall in 48 hours
Article Text:
In 48 hours, torrential rainfall hit Uttar Pradesh, causing devastating consequences that claimed 81 lives and injured 62





LUCKNOW: At least 81 people have lost their lives, and 62 others have been injured so far as incessant rain battered large parts of Uttar Pradesh between Sept 25 and Sept 27, causing widespread destruction across the state.The state has also recorded the deaths of 154 animals, while damage to crops is still being assessed.According to a situation report prepared by UP Relief Commissioner Hrishikesh Bhaskar Yashod’s office, Sitapur was the worst-affected district in terms of fatalities, reporting seven deaths. Lakhimpur Kheri, Bahraich and Balrampur recorded five deaths each, while Ayodhya, Maharajganj and Gorakhpur reported four fatalities each.Among the injured, Hardoi reported the highest number of injuries at seven, followed by Mainpuri and Shravasti with five each. Four people in Barabanki and three each in Sitapur and Lakhimpur Kheri also suffered injuries in rain-related incidents.A total of 154 animal deaths were reported across the state, with Hardoi accounting for the highest number at 28.Property damage was extensive, with 2,254 houses reported to be damaged.The report said that Uttar Pradesh received an average of 66.5 mm of rainfall during the 48-hour period against the normal 7.6 mm, representing 775% excess rainfall.Out of the state’s 75 districts, 56 recorded “large excess” rainfall. Farrukhabad registered the highest rainfall deviation at 7,385% above normal, followed by Kannauj (5,664%), Shahjahanpur (4,408%), Hamirpur (4,240%) and Mahoba (4,100%).“Assessment of crop losses is still underway as district administrations continue to carry out rescue, relief and damage assessment operations in affected areas,” Yashod said.
Article Summary: In 48 hours, torrential rainfall hit Uttar Pradesh, causing devastating consequences. At least 81 people have lost their lives, and 62 others have been injured so far. The state has also recorded the deaths of 154 animals, while damage to crops is still being assessed.

Article Title: 'Crushed man's head with stones': How Delhi murder accused evaded arrest for 24 years
Article Text:
A man named Firoj has been arrested after evading capture for 24 years.A man named Firoj has been arrested after evading capture for 24 years.

To avenge brother





NEW DELHI: A 24-year-long manhunt, which began with a highly decomposed body being found in a DDA forest, ended with the accused being arrested from Gurgaon by Delhi Police's Crime Branch. The accused, Firoj, had been absconding for over two decades after murdering a man to avenge an old family-related vendetta.On Feb 18, 2002, the decomposed body of 35-year-old Kalaam Ansari was found, covered with stones, inside the DDA forest near Tughlaqabad Fort. His head had been completely crushed. The deceased was identified as a resident of West Champaran, Bihar.During the investigation, police found Ansari had come to Delhi in 2001 for employment along with the murder accused, Firoj. One year later, on Feb 15, 2002, Firoj took Ansari to the forest near Tughlaqabad and crushed his head with stones, a senior police officer said.As per police, Ansari’s sister and Firoj’s brother, Saahbjan, were married and lived in the deceased’s village in West Champaran. Saahbjan had a dispute with his wife, who had refused to accompany him outside her village. Following this, Saahbjan committed suicide in front of the deceased’s house.Firoj suspected Ansari’s family had driven his brother to kill himself and had allegedly expressed his intention to take revenge.“One year after the duo came to Delhi in search of a job, Firoj took Ansari to the forest near Tughlaqabad and crushed his head with stones in 2002. He then returned to Bihar and started giving misleading information regarding the deceased’s whereabouts. When the murder came to light three days later, Firoj absconded and remained untraceable for nearly 24 years,” said DCP Harsh Indora.Considering the prolonged evasion of the accused and the heinous crime committed, Crime Branch undertook the task of tracing and arresting Firoj.Leads were developed by analysing old records, current data and sustained field efforts. After multiple visits to Bihar, 30 raids at suspected locations and a painstaking reconstruction of the accused’s trail conducted over two months, the police finally arrested Firoj from a ready-made garment factory in IMT Manesar, Gurgaon.Firoj, who is now 48 years old, had been working in the factory as a tailor for the past two years. After the murder, he had cut off ties with his native village and managed to conceal his identity for decades, and eventually shifted to Gurgaon, where he had been working at different places. He is married and has four children.Further investigation by the police is in progress.
Article Summary: Accused, Firoj, had been absconding for over two decades after murdering a man to avenge an old family-related vendetta. On Feb 18, 2002, the decomposed body of 35-year-old Kalaam Ansari was found, covered with stones, inside the DDA forest near Tughlaqabad Fort.

Article Title: Kolkata woman 'assaulted, abused' at at five-star hotel nightclub, JW Marriott says venue is third-party run
Article Text:
A young woman reported an incident of assault and wrongful restraint at a nightclub early Sunday morning. (File pic)





KOLKATA: Pragati Maidan cops have arrested a 24-year-old man for allegedly wrongfully restraining, physically assaulting, and outraging the modesty of a young woman at a nightclub inside a prominent five star hotel located along the EM Bypass near Science City in the early hours of Sunday.The arrested suspect has been identified as Mohammed Rafey Azim (24), a resident of Bhukailash Road in Kidderpore and Tiljala Road in the Beniapukur area.According to police, the incident occurred around 2 am on Sunday, when the 20-year-old complainant, a resident of New Alipore , visited the disco located inside the five star property along with a group of eight friends.The victim stated in her complaint that while they were at the venue, the accused, aided and abetted by others, confronted her group. The suspect allegedly subjected the complainant to wrongful restraint, physically assaulted her, and used extremely filthy and abusive language intended to insult her modesty. Following the altercation and physical assault, the accused and his aides fled the scene.The police were alerted through an emergency call at the Dial 100 control room. A team from Pragati Maidan PS immediately rushed to the place of occurrence.Cops said the five star hotel administration helped them in collecting evidence when requested.According to additional CP (crime) Kunal Agarwal, cops arrested the accused as soon as they received the complaint. “After receiving the information from Toy Room Disco located inside JW Marriott Hotel through Dial 100, a team of Pragati Maidan PS visited the place and after examination requested the complainant to submit a complaint. Meanwhile, the complainant and her friends came to Pragati Maidan PS and submitted the plaint letter. On the basis of it, an FIR was started. After lodging the FIR and identifying the address of accused, a raid was conducted and the accused was arrested,” said Agarwal.Pragati Maidan Police registered charges under sections 74 (assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 79 (word, gesture, or act intended to insult modesty), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), and 54 (abettor present when offence is committed) of the BNS.Azim was arrested from his Tiljala Road residence around 11:40 am on Sunday.Gorav Arora, general manager, JW Marriott Kolkata, said: “Toy Room is a third-party managed outsourced venue and the hotel does not operate it. We will however continue to extend our cooperation to the concerned authorities.”
Article Summary: A young woman reported an incident of assault and wrongful restraint at a nightclub early Sunday morning. The suspect allegedly subjected the complainant to wrongful restraint, physically assaulted her, and used extremely filthy and abusive language intended to insult her modesty. Mohammed Rafey Azim was arrested from his Tiljala Road residence.

Article Title: ‘Shopping for free’: Videos show students looting LPU campus mall amid violent protest
Article Text:
Several videos from Lovely Professional University show students reportedly taking items from shops during protests.

CHANDIGARH: Several videos emerging from Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara appear to show students entering shops inside the university’s Uni Mall, picking up food, gadgets and other items amid the violent protests that rocked the campus on Sunday.In one video, a voice can be heard saying “free mein shopping, shopping done” as people move around inside a store.Another video shows a person pointing towards various items in the mall and saying, “What do you need? Order now, will get everything for you in free.”Also read: LPU Student Protest Live Updates Other visuals purportedly show students eating food items inside the mall, while another set of videos shows shops and other property damaged during the unrest.The videos could not be independently verified. It was also not immediately clear from the visuals whether all those seen taking items were students of LPU.The alleged looting came as protests at LPU over claims surrounding the alleged rape of a female student escalated into violence, with protesters vandalising property, attacking police vehicles and blocking NH-44.Police said protesters pelted stones at police personnel after they were asked to clear the highway blockade on Sunday evening.Two police vehicles were set on fire and several others were damaged, officials said. A number of policemen were injured in the clashes.Also read: Students atop MiG-23, military tank Videos circulating online also show damage to shops in the campus mall, an ATM kiosk and other university property. Some protesters were seen with their faces covered.According to police, messages about an alleged rape and the death by suicide of a female student had begun circulating on social media on Saturday night, following which students gathered outside a girls’ hostel. The protest later spread to the highway and other parts of the campus.Police said an FIR had been registered based on the complaint relating to the alleged rape and an SIT had been formed. Investigators said CCTV footage, forensic samples and call records would be examined as part of the probe.LPU, however, has denied the rape allegations being circulated on campus, describing them as “false, baseless and fabricated rumours”. The university said it would cooperate with the investigation.A student claimed that the situation had gone beyond the students’ protest and alleged that outsiders and “goons” had entered the university.“The university's stand is that the students should stay safe. It is better for them to stay inside their hostels and stay safe from the locals and goons who have come. Instead of roaming outside, if they want to protest, they can do it peacefully,” the student said.The student further alleged that several students had confronted those involved in the violence and claimed that the university hall had been damaged, the CS building set on fire and the admission block vandalised.Also read: Abhijeet Dipke's 1st reaction on LPU unrest The unrest also followed discussions around the death by suicide of a Telangana student at LPU around a fortnight earlier. Police said the student’s mobile phone had been sent for forensic examination and further action would depend on the findings.The protests continued through Sunday, with students blocking NH-44 for several hours. Police eventually used a lathi charge to clear the blockade after negotiations failed, following which students allegedly retaliated with stone-pelting.Amid the violence, students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23 aircraft and a military tank displayed on the campus.LPU has suspended classes for 10 days from Monday and postponed midterm examinations until further notice.While some students alleged that outsiders were responsible for the looting, arson and vandalism, police said several people involved in the violence had their faces covered.The exact identities of those involved in the alleged looting and damage are expected to be established through CCTV footage and the police investigation.
Article Summary: Several videos from Lovely Professional University show students reportedly taking items from shops during protests. The alleged looting came as protests at LPU over claims surrounding the alleged rape of a female student escalated into violence. Police said protesters pelted stones at police personnel after they were asked to clear the highway blockade.

Article Title: Fake medicine racket: Prime suspect arrested at Bengaluru airport after landing from Sharjah
Article Text:
R Prashanth Babu, a medical representative, was caught at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport as part of a major police operation targeting a fake drug network spanning multiple states

BENGALURU: A special investigation team probing a multi-state fake drug racket arrested one of its prime suspects, R Prashanth Babu, at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport early Monday.Prashanth, a medical representative and resident of Papareddypalya in Bengaluru, was arrested after he landed from Sharjah around 5.30am.The arrest comes after police and health department officials busted the racket on August 18 this year. The operation was being run from an unlicensed facility near Tavarekere in Bidadi, in Ramanagara-Bengaluru South district. Drug enforcement officials and police seized spurious and expired medicines, packaging material and drug-filling equipment worth around Rs 5 crore.Police have so far arrested eight accused, including alleged kingpin Veeresh Kumar Jain, who ran the Krupa Health Care unit at Minerva Circle.The racket came to light after a labourer in C K Tandya village near Dodderi noticed discarded medicine waste, including vials, tubes and powder, dumped in a field. He alerted Shivaraj, a local police constable from Tavarekere police station.Shivaraj visited the spot in plain clothes, collected samples and informed senior officials.Based on the information, the Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA), along with local police, raided a farmhouse in Kurubara Karenahalli near the Bidadi toll gate.Investigators found that the operators were running an unlicensed manufacturing, repackaging and relabelling unit.The racket procured cheap, substandard generic medicines, expired medicines and low-cost cancer drugs from illegal manufacturing units across multiple states, including Telangana and Himachal Pradesh.The medicines were transferred into new vials and packages at the Bidadi farmhouse.The operators allegedly used forged labels, stamps and boxes bearing the names of prominent multinational pharmaceutical brands, including Pfizer and Kupa Healthcare, to sell the medicines as expensive, premium products.
Article Summary: R Prashanth Babu, a medical representative, was arrested at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport. The arrest comes after police and health department officials busted the racket on August 18 this year. The operation was being run from an unlicensed facility near Tavarekere in Bidadi, in Ramanagara- Bengaluru South district.

Article Title: ‘Harassed by math teacher for 3 months’: Ghaziabad girl dies after falling from 10th floor
Article Text:
A 13-year-old girl from Sahibabad fell from the 10th floor of a building and died.





GHAZIABAD: A 13-year-old girl died after falling from the 10th floor of a residential building in Sahibabad on Saturday night.Her family alleged that a schoolteacher had harassed her and that she had recorded everything in her diary.According to police, the deceased a resident of Gulmohar society in Sahibabad. Her father is a businessman in the city.A senior police officer said that the deceased was a student of class 7th of a private school in Sahibabad.Late on Saturday evening, the deceased had left the flat after telling her mother that she would return in a while. Shortly afterward, they were informed that she had fallen from the 10th floor.When her mother reached downstairs, a doctor living in the society was giving CPR to her daughter. After this, the student was taken by car to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared her dead during treatment after a short while.Acting on the information, police reached the spot, took the student’s body into custody and sent it for postmortem. After the postmortem on Saturday, police handed over the body to the family, and late in the evening the family performed the student’s last rites at the cremation ground on the Hindon riverbank.A family member said that the girl was harassed by her school math teacher for the last three months. She mentioned everything in her diary. Some days ago, an internal exam had been held at the school and the answer sheets had been shown to the students on Friday. She scored 30 marks in math after which she was angry and scared.Rijual, DCP of Trans-Hindon said police had not found any suicide note at her house. The family had neither lodged a complaint nor shown police any writing by the girl.“The body was sent for autopsy and reports are awaited,” he said.
Article Summary: A 13-year-old girl died after falling from the 10th floor of a residential building in Sahibabad on Saturday night. Her family alleged that a schoolteacher had harassed her and that she had recorded everything in her diary. The body was sent for autopsy and reports are awaited, police said.

Article Title: 'We call it kidnapping': CJP's Ashutosh Ranka calls Assam Police action completely illegal
